hypotheses: A surjection F→G of sheaves of sets on a site C.
conclusions: The parallel projections F×_G F⇒F with F→G form a coequalizer diagram.

hypotheses: A covering family {U_i→U} of a site C.
conclusions: The map from the coproduct of representables h_{U_i} to h_U becomes surjective after sheafification.

hypotheses: A site C and E⊂Ob(C) such that every object has a covering by objects in E; a sheaf F.
conclusions: There is a coequalizer diagram F1⇒F0→F in sheaves with F0 and F1 coproducts of associated representables h_U# for U∈E.

hypotheses: A site C and a sheaf F; optionally a covering family of generators E⊂Ob(C).
conclusions: F can be expressed as a colimit of associated representables h_{U_i}#.
If every object is covered by elements of E, the U_i may all be chosen in E.

hypotheses: A continuous functor u:C→D of sites and a sheaf F on D.
conclusions: The presheaf u^p F=F∘u is a sheaf on C.

hypotheses: A continuous functor u:C→D of sites and U∈Ob(C).
conclusions: u_s(h_U#) is canonically isomorphic to h_{u(U)}#.

hypotheses: Three sites and continuous functors u:C2→C1 and v:C3→C2, each defining morphisms of sites.
conclusions: The composite u∘v is continuous and defines a morphism of sites C1→C3.

hypotheses: A continuous functor u:C→D of sites; each category (I^u_V)^opp is filtered.
conclusions: u induces a morphism of sites D→C, equivalently its sheafification-assisted left adjoint u_s is exact.
lemma-directed-morphism.review_note: Indexing category definition from §5 is explicitly supplied; no assumptions of earlier lemmas carry over.

hypotheses: A continuous u:C→D with final object X of C mapped to final D-object, and fibre products in C preserved by u.
conclusions: u induces a morphism of sites D→C, i.e. u_s is exact.

hypotheses: A morphism of sites f:D→C corresponding to continuous u:C→D, and an object V of D.
conclusions: V has a covering {V_j→V} each term of which maps to u(U_j) for some U_j∈C.

hypotheses: A morphism of sites f:D→C induced by continuous u:C→D.
conclusions: The adjoint pair (f^-1=u_s,f_*=u^s) defines a morphism of topoi Sh(D)→Sh(C).

hypotheses: A site C and object U; conditions (1) quasi-compactness, (2) every covering has a finite covering refining it, (3) every covering admits a finite subfamily which is a covering.
conclusions: (3) implies (2), which implies (1); neither converse holds in general.

hypotheses: A site C and object U.
conclusions: Quasi-compactness of U is equivalent to finite subcoproduct surjectivity of every coproduct of sheaves onto h_U#.

hypotheses: A site C.
conclusions: A surjection h_U#→h_V# induced by U→V preserves quasi-compactness from U to V.
Any surjection of sheaves F→G carries quasi-compactness from F to G.

hypotheses: A positive integer n and n quasi-compact sheaves F_i on a site.
conclusions: Their finite coproduct is quasi-compact.

hypotheses: A site C, a filtered diagram of sheaves, and the canonical map Ψ from colimit of global sections to global sections of the colimit.
conclusions: (1) Injective transitions imply Ψ injective.
(2) Quasi-compactness of Sh(C) implies Ψ injective.
(3) Quasi-compactness plus injective transitions implies Ψ is an isomorphism.
(4) The specified generating set S with quasi-compact self-products implies Ψ bijective.

hypotheses: A site C, ordinal β, an ordinal-indexed system of sheaves, and an object U.
conclusions: The evaluation map from the colimit of sections to the sections of the colimit is bijective under a cofinality-size condition.
lemma-colimit-over-ordinal-sections.hold_reason: The statement says 'cofinality of β is large enough' without a value or quantified threshold, so cannot certify a precise standalone hypothesis.
lemma-colimit-over-ordinal-sections.review_note: Determine the actual cardinal threshold or revise the source claim; no numeric bound is specified in the source statement.

hypotheses: A cofiltered inverse system of sites with finite covering-index sets, compatible transition morphisms, its constructed colimit site C, an index i, an object U_i, and sheaf F on C_i.
conclusions: The canonical functor u_i defines a site morphism f_i and the evaluation of f_i^-1 F at u_i(U_i) is a colimit of f_a^-1 F evaluated at u_a(U_i).

hypotheses: A cofiltered inverse system of sites; compatible sheaves F_i and morphisms φ_a satisfying φ_c=φ_b◦f_b^-1φ_a.
conclusions: For each index i and object X_i the indicated colimit of F_j(u_a(X_i)) identifies with the colimit sheaf F at u_i(X_i).

hypotheses: A cofiltered inverse system of sites with constructed colimit site C and a sheaf F on C.
conclusions: F is the colimit of f_i^-1 f_{i,*} F, along canonical transition maps satisfying the same cocycle compatibility as the previous colimit lemma.

hypotheses: A functor u:C→D and the presheaf functors u^p and _p u.
conclusions: The functor _p u is right adjoint to u^p via the displayed natural Hom identity.

hypotheses: Functors u:C→D and v:D→C, with v right adjoint to u.
conclusions: The pullback of h_V by u is h_{v(V)}.
The category I^v_U has an initial object.
The category _V^u I has a final object.
The right and left Kan extension identities _p u=v^p and u^p=v_p hold.

hypotheses: A cocontinuous u:C→D and a sheaf F on C.
conclusions: The right Kan-extension presheaf _p u F is a sheaf on D, denoted _s u F.

hypotheses: A cocontinuous functor u:C→D of sites.
conclusions: Sheafified pullback G↦(u^p G)# is an exact left adjoint to _s u on sheaves.
lemma-exact-cocontinuous.review_note: The notation _s u comes from the preceding source lemma as the sheaf-valued _p u functor.
